edge_explainer: A real de-rate on a real quality business that has stopped growing, and the deceleration was disclosed by management first. Operating profit set an all-time peak in FY2025 at GBP 32.06m (FY21 19.2 -> FY22 24.7 -> FY23 27.8 -> FY24 30.6 -> FY25 32.1) at an 18% margin with net cash, yet the stock is 23.7% lower over a year. But the growth rate collapsed +12.6% -> +10.1% -> +4.7% -> +0.3% at H1 FY26, revenue peaked back in FY2023, operating cash flow FELL 19.7% to GBP 33.2m while profit rose, and the Chairman explicitly warned H2 growth 'remains a challenge, especially considering the strong second half achieved in 2024/25'. So 7.8x EV/EBIT is a trough multiple on PEAK earnings - the bear case needs no further de-rate, only for earnings to follow the revenue already falling. Because management volunteered the caution alongside a record print, there is no takeaway-vs-data divergence: on the honesty axis this is CLEAN and therefore correctly priced. Honestly disclosed deceleration is not alpha.
